guitar.evidence: Trained knowledge: Gary Clark Jr. is well known for using semi-hollow guitars, notably an Epiphone Casino and later a signature Gibson/Epiphone ES-335-style model.
guitar.notes: Well-documented modern blues-rock guitarist gear — should not have been unknown.

tone.target: gated fuzzed blues-rock lead with wah bite
tone.profile: gated fuzzed blues-rock lead with wah bite
tone.summary: A fuzz-driven signal chain utilizing a classic British amp model and wah to achieve gritty, singing blues leads.

rig.name: Gary Clark Jr. - Bright Lights - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and unwanted noise inherent in high-gain fuzz tones.
Provide initial grit and boost the signal into the fuzz stage.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used as a foundational dirt source, mimicking an early overdrive for blues context.

alternatives.reason: Similar function but might be too clean.

blocks.purpose: Deliver the primary fuzzed saturation and aggressive grit required for the lead tone.
Provide the signature wah sweeps and vocal bite essential for blues lead work.
Simulate the classic British Marshall-style power amp backbone for rock grit.
blocks.gap: The UK 45 provides the necessary high-gain, mid-focused character without sounding overly modern or metal.

alternatives.reason: Could be used for a slightly cleaner classic rock feel.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic British cabinet voicing to complement the Marshall-style amp.
Add subtle thickening and 'singing' sustain to the lead lines.
blocks.gap: Chorus is used subtly here, rather than for obvious 80s effect, to enhance sustain and round out the tone.

alternatives.reason: Too rhythmic; Chorus provides better sustained wash.

blocks.purpose: Add a short, tasteful echo to enhance the lead lines and give space.
blocks.gap: The delay is kept relatively subtle (low feedback/mix) to complement the fuzz without sounding dated.

alternatives.reason: Too warm; Digital Delay offers more precise control for blues leads.

blocks.purpose: Provide a natural sense of space and depth for the lead passages.
blocks.gap: Room reverb is preferred over Plate/Spring as it adds a more organic, less artificial ambience suitable for blues-rock.

alternatives.reason: Can sound too bright or metallic with heavy fuzz.

blocks.purpose: Final output level control to ensure the signal is balanced for FRFR monitoring.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR to better capture the raw, mid-focused aggression of a Marshall stack for blues lead work.

proposals.reason: Enhance the aggressive, mid-focused bite needed for Gary Clark Jr.'s style.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and punch in the upper mids.
